short: Text+ultrasound fusion in DNN-TTS (M06) is standard: test MCD gain 0.015-0.229 dB on 8 speakers, but test BAP and voicing worsen; naturalness claimed without a listening test (M12 behind).
position: The paper changes one component: the acoustic model of a Merlin DNN-TTS receives 128 PCA coefficients of the ultrasound tongue image next to the linguistic features (M06) [@csapo2021txtult]. The network is the field's usual frame-wise fully connected regression, so M06 is standard; the pairing is new only in its sensor, as the paper's own Sec. 1.3 scopes it after EMA-based articulatory TTS. Test MCD falls for all 8 speakers, but by 0.015 to 0.229 dB, about 2% on average, from one run per speaker on roughly 10 test sentences (Table 1, Sec. 2.1; inference). On the test set BAP error rises for 6 of 8 speakers and voicing error for all 8 (Tables 2, 5; inference), so the excitation claim fails. Naturalness is claimed (Abstract, Sec. 5) without the listening test the same group ran in at least 4 earlier ultrasound-to-speech studies (M12, behind). The ultrasound input is a recording of the very utterance being scored, and the system needs text and articulation together, which the authors concede rules out TTS or silent-speech use (Sec. 5).
